bullets.title: Iran escalation drives WTI +5-6%, triggers broad risk-off selloff
bullets.body: US launched strikes on 80+ Iranian targets; Trump declared the Iran MOU 'over' and revoked oil-selling licenses. WTI surged ~5-6% to ~$74/bbl on Strait of Hormuz disruption fears, while S&P 500 futures fell 0.85-1.5%, European markets dropped 1.5-2%, and 10-year Treasury yields rose to ~4.57%.

bullets.title: Momentum/AI infrastructure basket down ~20% from June peak — rotation, not de-risking
bullets.body: The High Beta Momentum basket (85% correlated to AI infrastructure) fell ~20% peak-to-trough in ~14 days, matching the 7th-largest drawdown in a decade. JPM and multiple desks characterize this as rotation-driven (Energy/Staples leading, semis/Mag7 selling) rather than fundamental de-grossing; volume/flow data show retail dip-buying, not panic. Mag7 is now at 10-year low relative valuation vs SPX.

bullets.title: FOMC minutes due 14:00 ET today; hawkish tone expected under new Fed Chair Warsh
bullets.body: June FOMC minutes release will be scrutinized for the statement overhaul and hawkish dots under Chair Warsh. Separately, one technical view targets the 2-year Treasury yield reaching 5%, noting that every point on the yield curve currently sits above the Fed Funds rate — a pattern that has historically preceded rate hikes.

bullets.title: Q2 earnings season setup: 20%+ growth expected, options pricing modest moves
bullets.body: BCA Research raised S&P 500 2026 PT to 8100 on $330 EPS (up from $308), with Q2 earnings expected to deliver 20%+ YoY growth for the second straight quarter. Options imply ±5.1% earnings-day moves vs last quarter's realized ±5.4%; EPS beat rate hit recent highs last quarter (+86bps avg return, highest since 2012). 46% of S&P 500 companies raised guidance last quarter, 4th consecutive quarter of improvement.

bullets.title: DRAM contract prices up 20-30% Q3, NAND up 35-40% Q3 — memory supply shortage deepening through 1H28
bullets.body: Taiwan Economic Daily reports DRAM contracts up 20-30% Q3 and NAND up 35-40% Q3. Jefferies and MS note the memory supply-demand gap is severe through 1H28 as AI investment rises from $800B (2026) to $1.5T (2028); Samsung 3Q26 pricing up ~22-25%. Memory makers are prioritizing HBM/DDR5 over legacy nodes with reduced legacy capacity planned for 2026.

bullets.title: SOXX in ~18% drawdown; semi cap weakness seen as positioning-driven, not fundamental
bullets.body: SOXX is in an ~18% drawdown matching November 2025 and Iran war lows. Citi argues semi cap weakness (AMAT down 25% in past week) is positioning/derisking-driven, not fundamental deterioration. Key upcoming catalysts: ASML results July 15 and TSMC results July 16. LO flows in semicap paused after 6 weeks of buying; HF selling for 15 days.

bullets.title: TSMC 3Q26 revenue guidance expected +10-12% QoQ, above consensus; FY27 capex $75B
bullets.body: Jefferies and GS expect TSMC to guide 3Q26 revenue +10-12% QoQ (above high-single-digit consensus) when it reports July 16. Arizona fab GM already at 50% with 90% yield; FY27 gross margin seen reaching 70%. FY27 capex forecast at $75B vs FY26 target of $56-57B; N3 capacity to reach 210kwpm by end FY27.

bullets.title: AI capex supercycle intact: hyperscalers raising spend, AMZN issuing $25B+ in bonds
bullets.body: GS raised AMZN AWS revenue estimates 7% above Street for 2027; GOOGL cumulative capex now $790B expected over 2026-28; META capex raised to ~$534B over 2026-28. AMZN is raising at least $25B in bond sales for AI capex; Semianalysis forecasts $7T AI debt outstanding by 2029. META is not signaling any AI spending slowdown despite stock weakness.

bullets.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 launches Thursday after Trump admin approval; China tightening AI model access
bullets.body: Trump administration approved OpenAI to launch GPT-5.6 globally Thursday. Simultaneously, China is considering restricting overseas access to domestic AI models and warned of 'back-door' risks from Anthropic's Claude Code; Chinese firms plan to allocate 46% of AI accelerator budgets to domestic products over next 12 months vs 30% today. DeepSeek is quietly developing custom inference silicon.

bullets.title: SK Hynix $28-29B ADR listing Friday; expected 8% premium, likely funded via semi rotation
bullets.body: SK Hynix's massive US ADR listing is multiple times oversubscribed and expected to price Thursday, trading Friday. Jefferies flags the listing is likely funded via rotation out of regional semiconductor exposure, adding near-term pressure to the semi cohort.

bullets.title: Digital ad Q2 trends solid: direct response strongest, June rebound after muted start
bullets.body: GS and multiple desks flag digital ad Q2 fundamentals as solid, with strongest trends in performance/direct response advertising, AI automation, short-form video, and commerce. Pattern showed muted early quarter then June rebound; month-to-month volatility elevated. META and GOOGL remain preferred large-cap ideas heading into earnings.

bullets.title: AI momentum unwind risk elevated: S&P momentum index +70% vs market since 2024, nearing dotcom levels
bullets.body: Jefferies warns the S&P 500 momentum index has outperformed the broader market by >70% since 2024, nearing dotcom-run levels, with the current run supported almost entirely by the AI theme. KOSPI VIX hit 97 with trading halts driven by retail/leveraged ETF participation. Jefferies screens favor quality/low-risk stocks and software for near-term mean reversion.

bullets.title: AI corporate adoption accelerating: 40% of adopters cite quantifiable benefits in 2Q26, up from 21% a year ago
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley data shows share of AI adopters citing quantifiable benefits rose to 40% in 2Q26 from 21% in 2Q25; for broader S&P 500, ~25% mentioned measurable AI benefits vs 14% in 2Q25. Tech sector leads at 51%. About 10% of S&P 500 discussed AI's labor impact, with revenue-headcount decoupling seeing the largest increase.

bullets.title: Microsoft shifting Excel/Outlook AI prompts to internal MAI models, away from OpenAI/Anthropic
bullets.body: Multiple sources (JPM, GS, Wolfe) confirm Microsoft is routing some Excel and Outlook AI prompts to internally-built MAI models to reduce inference costs as volumes explode. This reinforces the inference cost compression narrative and puts pressure on OpenAI/Anthropic's enterprise revenue trajectory.

bullets.title: AAPL testing China-made CXMT DRAM chips for China-sold devices
bullets.body: Apple has begun testing CXMT (China state-backed) DRAM chips for China-sold devices, per multiple desks including GS and Jefferies. Chinese PC OEMs (Lenovo, ASUS, MSI, Gigabyte, Acer) are also validating CXMT DRAM and YMTC NAND as Samsung/SK Hynix prioritize HBM for AI servers, potentially creating a bifurcated memory supply chain.

bullets.title: EU court upholds Apple's gatekeeper designation; DMA compliance obligations and 10%-of-turnover fines remain
bullets.body: The EU General Court dismissed Apple's challenge to its designation as gatekeeper under the Digital Markets Act for App Store and iOS. Apple's iMessage challenge was found inadmissible. An appeal to the Court of Justice on points of law only is possible within ~2.5 months.

bullets.title: May trade deficit $77.6B, slightly better than consensus; 2Q GDP tracking +2.2% annualized
bullets.body: The May trade deficit widened to $77.6B, slightly better than consensus. GS is tracking 2Q GDP at +2.2% annualized with domestic final sales at +2.0%, suggesting a still-solid macro backdrop heading into earnings season.

bullets.title: Oil medium-term outlook: Morgan Stanley sees 2027 Brent glut driving prices to $70/bbl by 2H27
bullets.body: Despite the current geopolitical spike, Morgan Stanley moved its 2027 Dated Brent forecast from flat $80/b to $75/b in 1H27 and $70/b in 2H27, citing physical glut from high US exports and low Chinese imports. OPEC+ is also raising August production by 188k bopd, prioritizing market share over price.

bullets.title: Large-cap bank earnings setup positive: GS, JPM, BNY, STT expected to surprise to upside
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley previews 2Q26 large-cap bank earnings as Attractive, flagging likely upside surprises at GS (Global Banking & Markets revenue), JPM (NII guidance), BNY (NII), and STT (medium-term ROTCE guidance). IB fee revenue for 8 global banks was up +38% YoY in 2Q, led by ECM +89% and Advisory +26%.

bullets.title: Cybersecurity Q2 channel checks: closed above plan, slight improvement in sales cycles
bullets.body: Roth channel checks show Q2 closed above plan with a slight improvement in sales cycles vs April. PANW improved to +10% above plan (from 5-9%) driven by CyberArk cross-sell; CRWD eased to 5-9% above plan (from 10%) as new logos were light and SentinelOne pressed aggressively in SMB. FTNT was at plan with FortiBleed incident creating deal drag that may extend into Q3.
